claims.claim: A distinct version 2 source-control bootstrap intent and durable handoff bind the legacy generation, unchanged source-control commit and pin, authorized TASK, Executor, and exact target. A focused test stages it without a prospective target-control or pin commit.
The target consumer validates the durable handoff and running target source, then delegates the bound TASK to the existing run_task with synchronize=False.
Production activation defaults to None. The new target consumer does not approve its own SHA, and the historical TASK-198 bootstrap target remains fixed at 83115b26df85a7ad6643f317833e18b18586bdbe.

The new path reconciles active and terminal RUNs, rejects mismatched or stale state, and prevents a second Executor call on reentry. Pre-edge rejection creates no RUN or FAILURE and invokes no Executor.

Focused new-path tests passed for identity binding, closed and injected activation, unsafe control, target mismatch, replay, and stale upstream. Two focused existing bootstrap and migrate regression tests passed; the new path reuses their bounded transport and cleanup code.
Brain Portability documentation records capability publication, a separate exact-SHA activation TASK, and later explicit BP-9 adoption; it claims no downstream migration from this TASK.
